title: How to Make $50 Per Day Betting on Sports (The Math)
summary: Sports betting tipster claims a repeatable system of heavy-favorite player props with a five-figure bankroll yields steady daily profit; sells daily picks.

assertions.quote: as long as you have an edge, the long term, you're actually going to turn a profit. It just takes time.

verdicts.note: The arithmetic is correct, but sustaining a true edge against sharp lines is rare and books limit winners.
As a conditional statement this is basic expected-value arithmetic; the hard part, which the claim does not deny, is having and keeping such an edge.

assertions.quote: The profit is at player props.

verdicts.note: Derivative markets are less efficient than main lines, but limits are lower and books restrict prop winners quickly.
Props and other low-volume markets are widely documented as less efficient than main lines, though books offset this with low limits and quick restrictions.

assertions.quote: If you don't have no money, then you go into the lottery system

verdicts.note: Bankroll scales any real edge, but the premise that the edge exists is unproven.

assertions.quote: there's no way anybody could tell you otherwise because this is tracked every single day

verdicts.note: Unaudited trackers can omit bets, and a few months of results are dominated by variance.

assertions.quote: trying to put 20, 30, 40 dollars on them to try to win thousands of dollars, which they never do

verdicts.note: Parlay hold percentages reported by books are several times those on straight bets.

assertions.quote: they've lost a couple thousand dollars without even knowing it
